name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

🎲 MYRIAD

Propose K varied attempts at one task, score them with a deterministic verifier, and compound the group-relative advantage — critic-free self-play, no training run.
MYRIAD is self-play for LLM agents. Given a task, it proposes K attempts along fixed, distinct reasoning angles, fans them out through any model you inject, scores each with a DETERMINISTIC verifier you control (never a model grading its own work), and computes each attempt's group-relative advantage with critic-free GRPO. The best variant is the answer; the spread becomes a lesson you can distill into a policy. No gradient step, no training loop, no judge model — just structured variation plus grounded scoring, fail-open at every stage.

self-play · reinforcement-learning · grpo · verifier · llm-agents · zero-deps

--- ## Why MYRIAD Sampling a model once gives you one draw from its distribution. MYRIAD turns one task into a small population: K attempts along fixed angles (direct, step-by-step, adversarial, minimal, …) so the variation is deliberate and reproducible, not random temperature. Each attempt is scored by a verifier YOU write — a unit test, a checker, an exact-match — so the reward is grounded, never a model judging itself. GRPO then normalizes the rewards into group-relative advantages (Â = (R−μ)/σ) with no learned critic, giving you a clean training signal you can distill into a policy (pairs beautifully with a task-level RL brain). The best variant is your answer; the worst is a labeled negative. It's the compounding core of self-improving agents, in two files, with no training infrastructure. --- ## What it does | Module | What it does | Signal | |---|---|---| | **self-play cycle** | Propose K angle-varied attempts → fan-out → deterministic score → GRPO advantage → distill | one task, K draws | | **group-advantage** | Critic-free GRPO normalization Â = (R−μ)/σ over the K rewards | pure, deterministic | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T["task"] --> P["propose K\nfixed angles"] P --> F["fan-out\n(your model)"] F --> S["deterministic\nverifier → reward"] S --> GA["GRPO advantage\nÂ = (R−μ)/σ"] GA --> B["best variant\n= answer"] GA --> D["distill\n(policy sink)"] classDef acc fill:#4a1f2b,stroke:#F25C7A,color:#fff; class S acc; class GA acc; ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. no install needed — pure Node builtins node lib/group-advantage.cjs # GRPO self-test node lib/myriad.cjs # self-play smoke test (stubbed model, no calls) # 2. run a real self-play cycle with a deterministic verifier node examples/demo.cjs # 3. in your code # const { myriadCycle } = require('./lib/myriad.cjs'); # const r = await myriadCycle({ task, variants: 6, # model: async (prompt) => callYourLLM(prompt), # verifier: (out, task) => scoreIt(out, task) }); // -> { output, bestReward, trajectories } ``` > MYRIAD only makes model calls when you inject a `model` function (or set MYRIAD_MODEL); with no model it fans out to empty outputs so the cycle logic stays testable and $0. An optional ./data ledger records cycles for a distill step; it's gitignored and auto-created. Every stage is fail-open — a cycle never crashes. --- ## See it run

--- ## Repository layout ``` myriad/ ├── lib/ │ ├── myriad.cjs ← the self-play cycle (propose → fan-out → score → GRPO → distill) │ └── group-advantage.cjs ← critic-free GRPO advantage (pure math + self-test) ├── examples/ │ ├── demo.cjs ← a real cycle with a deterministic verifier, best-variant selection │ └── model-echo.cjs ← a zero-dep example model function (swap for a real LLM) └── data/ ← optional cycle ledger for distillation (gitignored, auto-created) ``` --- ## Concepts | Concept | Meaning | |---|---| | **Self-play cycle** | Propose K attempts at one task → fan out → score deterministically → compute group advantage → distill the winners. | | **Angle-varied proposals** | Each attempt approaches the task from a different declared angle, so the group explores instead of cloning itself. | | **Deterministic verifier** | YOU supply the scorer — a test, a checker, a measurable outcome. The system never grades its own homework. | | **Group advantage** | Critic-free GRPO normalization Â = (R−μ)/σ over the K rewards — relative signal with no critic model. | | **Distill sink** | Winners (and their advantages) flow to an optional onResult sink plus a ./data ledger for downstream learning. | | **Injectable model** | A model function or MYRIAD_MODEL env — the cycle runs end-to-end with an empty stub, $0. | --- ## Design principles 1. **Deliberate variation, not random.** K fixed angles make the population reproducible and meaningful — you can reason about what each attempt tried. 2. **Grounded reward, never self-judged.** The verifier is yours (a test, a checker); a model never scores its own work. 3. **A signal without a training run.** Critic-free GRPO turns the K rewards into advantages you can distill — no gradient step, no infra. 4. **Fail-open everywhere.** Missing model, broken verifier, absent sink — each degrades gracefully; a cycle never crashes. ---

what it does

Self-play in two files.

01 / PROPOSE

Structured variation

One task becomes K attempts along fixed, ordered angles — direct, step-by-step, adversarial, minimal, and more. The variation is deliberate and reproducible (no random temperature), so the population is meaningful. Fan them out through any model you inject.

02 / VERIFY

Grounded reward, never self-judged

You supply the verifier — a unit test, a checker, an exact-match — and it scores each attempt in [0,1]. A model never grades its own output. No verifier? A bounded non-empty heuristic keeps the cycle running; swap in a real one to get real signal.

03 / COMPOUND

A training signal, no training run

GRPO normalizes the K rewards into group-relative advantages with no learned critic. The best variant is your answer; the full group — with advantages and lessons — distills into whatever policy sink you plug in. Compounding self-improvement without a gradient step.

# MYRIAD — Architecture

MYRIAD is self-play for LLM agents. Given a task, it proposes K attempts along fixed, distinct reasoning angles, fans them out through any model you inject, scores each with a DETERMINISTIC verifier you control (never a model grading its own work), and computes each attempt's group-relative advantage with critic-free GRPO. The best variant is the answer; the spread becomes a lesson you can distill into a policy. No gradient step, no training loop, no judge model — just structured variation plus grounded scoring, fail-open at every stage.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["task"] --> P["propose K\nfixed angles"]
    P --> F["fan-out\n(your model)"]
    F --> S["deterministic\nverifier → reward"]
    S --> GA["GRPO advantage\nÂ = (R−μ)/σ"]
    GA --> B["best variant\n= answer"]
    GA --> D["distill\n(policy sink)"]
    classDef acc fill:#4a1f2b,stroke:#F25C7A,color:#fff;
    class S acc;
    class GA acc;
```

## How it fits together

MYRIAD is a self-play cycle over a shared GRPO primitive. `lib/group-advantage.cjs` is a pure, dependency-free critic-free advantage: given K rewards it returns Â = (R−μ)/σ (guarded so it never emits NaN/Infinity), plus mean and bestIndex. `lib/myriad.cjs::myriadCycle({ task, variants, model, verifier, ... })` runs one round: PROPOSE builds K prompts by appending fixed ordered angles to the task (deterministic — no random temperature); FAN-OUT calls your injected `model` function per variant (sequentially, so a heavy model channel is never oversubscribed) or, if none is given, resolves MYRIAD_MODEL, else fans out to empty outputs; SCORE runs your deterministic `verifier(output, task)` clamped to [0,1] (default: a bounded non-empty heuristic — never a model grading itself); GROUP-ADVANTAGE normalizes the rewards; DISTILL records the group (advantages + best/worst lessons) through an optional sink you pass as `onResult`, and/or appends to a ./data ledger. It returns the best variant's output plus per-trajectory rewards and advantages. Every stage past the group-advantage require is lazy and fail-open: a missing model, throwing verifier, or absent sink degrades rather than crashing the cycle.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **Deliberate variation, not random.** K fixed angles make the population reproducible and meaningful — you can reason about what each attempt tried.
2. **Grounded reward, never self-judged.** The verifier is yours (a test, a checker); a model never scores its own work.
3. **A signal without a training run.** Critic-free GRPO turns the K rewards into advantages you can distill — no gradient step, no infra.
4. **Fail-open everywhere.** Missing model, broken verifier, absent sink — each degrades gracefully; a cycle never crashes.
